games.name: Visual Pinball X VR
games.tagline: Real pinball tables in VR and mixed reality on Meta Quest 3 and PICO.
about: Visual Pinball X standalone for **Meta Quest 3** (OpenXR, Vulkan), based on vpinball 10.8.1. Stand in front of real and original tables, with the cabinet and backglass around you, or play them in your own room with passthrough.

A **PICO build** is available as well, with controller support for PICO Neo 3, PICO 4 and PICO G3, and it installs on Android 10 (PICO 4, Neo 3). It is **not tested on PICO hardware yet**: reports are very welcome.
features: 🆕 **Brand new: Table Downloader** (Meta Quest): pick tables from the Visual Pinball Collection on archive.org right in the headset (**+ → Download from Archive.org**). ROM, backglass and NVRAM are installed with the table, ready to play
**Main menu in VR:** the table library opens on a curved screen, point with a controller and pull the trigger. Left stick click switches between your room (mixed reality) and a black VR space
**Mixed Reality (passthrough):** see your real room around the table, switchable instantly while playing. The VR room of the table is hidden, so only the machine stands in your room
**Standard cabinet** for tables not built for VR: body, legs and backbox around the playfield, so the table stands in your room instead of floating
**Backglass for tables not built for VR:** rebuilt from the desktop backdrop, including working EM score reels
**VR room switch:** show or hide the VR room of any table from the menu, and cycle the rooms of the tables which offer some (also by holding the menu button)
Adjustable table position, angle, size and distance
Accidental Start presses are ignored while a ball is in play
The menu pauses the game
needs: Meta Quest 3, or PICO 4 / Neo 3 (untested)
Tables and ROMs: download them in the app (Meta Quest), or bring your own `.vpx` tables and ROMs
install: Sideload the APK for your headset with SideQuest or `adb install -r <apk>`: `VPinball-QuestVR-Beta-0.39.apk` for Meta Quest, `VPinball-PicoVR-Beta-0.6.apk` for PICO.
Start VPinball (*Library → Unknown Sources*) and get tables with **+ → Download from Archive.org** (Meta Quest): the table, its ROM and backglass are installed for you.

Or use your own tables: put each in its own folder, with its ROMs next to it (`VPinball/tables/<Table name>/<table>.vpx` and `VPinball/tables/<Table name>/pinmame/roms/<rom>.zip`), and select the `VPinball/tables` folder in the settings.

rows: Start game (hold 1 s while a ball is moving)
View mode: left stick = left/right & up/down, right stick = angle (press again to save). **Hold: reset view**
Size & distance mode: left stick = distance, right stick = size

notes: Williams / Bally / Data East tables show "Factory settings restored" on their very first start: quit once through the menu and start again.

Some VR tables ship with `Const VRRoom = 0`, which hides their cabinet. Put a copy of the table script next to the table as `<table name>.vbs` with `VRRoom` set to a room ("Ultra Minimal" is the lightest).
Updating from an earlier beta: install over it, settings and tables are kept.
The table downloader and the VR main menu are in the Meta Quest build for now. Some tables are several hundred MB: use a fast Wi-Fi connection.
The PICO build is untested: if it does not start, or the buttons are mapped differently, please open an issue on GitHub.
games.controls_note: Button names are those of the Meta Quest controllers, PICO controllers use the same layout.
games.credits: Based on [Visual Pinball](https://github.com/vpinball/vpinball) by the Visual Pinball development team.

games.name: Unreal Tournament VR
games.tagline: UT99 in VR, standalone on Meta Quest and PICO.
about: A standalone VR port for Meta Quest 2 / Pro / 3 / 3S (tested on Quest 3) and PICO 4 / Neo 3 of **Unreal Tournament (UT99)**, built on [Surreal Engine](https://github.com/dpjudas/SurrealEngine), a from-scratch reimplementation of Unreal Engine 1, with an OpenXR/Vulkan stereo renderer.
No game content is included, but UT99 is available **free and legally** from OldUnreal, and the app downloads and installs it for you on first launch.
PICO support is brand new and **not tested on PICO hardware yet**: reports are very welcome. One APK covers both makes.
features: Native OpenXR rendering at 72 Hz, snap turning, stick locomotion
Weapons held and aimed with the right controller, including UT's dual Enforcers
Sniper rifle zoom shown as a scope screen above the gun
Redeemer guided shell steered with the right controller
Installs side by side with Unreal Gold VR
Downloads and installs the free original game from OldUnreal on first launch: no file copying
Flat, readable menu panel; an on-screen keyboard pops up when you click a text field (e.g. your player name)
Correct lighting and colours in the headset, muzzle flash on the barrel of every weapon
needs: Meta Quest 2 / Pro / 3 / 3S, or PICO 4 / Neo 3 (untested)
Wi-Fi for the one-time game download (620 MB, free from [OldUnreal](https://www.oldunreal.com/downloads/unrealtournament/full-game-installers/)), or your own UT99 game files (469e and 436 work)
install: Sideload the APK with [SideQuest](https://sidequestvr.com/setup-howto) or `adb install -r`. SideQuest is a Quest tool, so on PICO use adb or whichever sideloader you already use.
Launch **Unreal Tournament VR** from *Unknown Sources* and grant "All files access".

On first launch a panel offers to download the free original Unreal Tournament GOTY disc (620 MB) from OldUnreal, the source Epic Games approved. Press **I agree - download and install**: it installs UT 436 with all maps and starts the game (Wi-Fi needed, about a minute).

Prefer your own files? Copy your UT99 `System`, `Maps`, `Textures`, `Sounds`, `Music` and `Help` folders to `/sdcard/SurrealEngineUT/` before the first launch (leave out `UnrealTournament.ini` / `User.ini`) and the download is skipped.

rows: Show / hide the on-screen keyboard (in menus)

notes: Bot AI is only partially implemented in Surreal Engine.
No dynamic lighting; some movers behave oddly.
No networking / multiplayer.

The PICO build is untested: if it does not start, or the controllers do nothing, please open an issue on GitHub. `adb logcat -s SurrealEngine-Log:*` shows how far it gets, which is the useful thing to paste in.

games.name: Descent 3 VR
games.tagline: Six degrees of freedom, from a real cockpit, on Meta Quest and PICO.
about: A VR port of the [Descent 3 open source engine](https://github.com/DescentDevelopers/Descent3) for Meta Quest and PICO, running standalone. You sit in a virtual cockpit: the ship flies on the Touch controllers while you look around freely. The world and the cockpit are rendered in stereo; menus, cutscenes and the flat HUD float in front of you.
features: Stereo world and cockpit with head tracking
Full ship control on the Touch controllers
Menus and dialogs fully usable with the controllers
Quest system keyboard for text fields like the pilot name
Runs at 90 Hz where available
needs: Meta Quest (Quest 3 tested), or PICO 4 / Neo 3 (untested)
Your own copy of Descent 3 (original CDs, GOG or Steam; v1.4 recommended)
install: Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r Descent3-VR-0.3-beta.apk`.
Copy all `.hog` files plus the `missions` and `movies` folders to `/sdcard/Android/data/com.descentdevelopers.descent3/files/`.

From GOG/Steam: after copying with adb, make the folders readable for the app with `adb shell "cd /sdcard/Android/data/com.descentdevelopers.descent3/files && find . -mindepth 1 -type d -exec chmod 2777 {} +"`.

From the original CDs: [quest/tools/stage_gamedata.sh](https://github.com/SgtBilko76/Descent3-VR/tree/quest-vr-port/quest/tools) in the source repository extracts the data from CD images and pushes it to the headset.
notes: **Uninstalling the app deletes the game data folder**: keep a copy of your game files.
After your ship is destroyed, pull a trigger or press A to continue.

The PICO build is untested: if it does not start, or the buttons are mapped differently, please open an issue on GitHub. `adb logcat -s Descent3:V` prints the runtime it found and the controller profile it bound, which is the useful thing to paste in.
Rear view and inventory have no controller buttons yet.
Some disc copies lack the music; pre-v1.4 data lacks a few images and sounds.
Multiplayer is untested.
games.credits: Based on the [Descent 3 open source engine](https://github.com/DescentDevelopers/Descent3) by the Descent community.

games.name: OpenXWA VR
games.tagline: Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance in a real cockpit, standalone on Meta Quest and PICO.
about: A VR port of [OpenXWA](https://github.com/elyosh/OpenXWA), the open source rebuild of *Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance*, running standalone. You sit in the 3D cockpit of your ship and look around freely while you fly with the Touch controllers. The concourse, briefings and cutscenes play on a big virtual screen.
features: Head-tracked stereo 3D cockpit and space in flight, including the hyperspace jump
Detailed 3D cockpits from X-Wing Revival for the X-Wing, Y-Wing, A-Wing, B-Wing, TIE Fighter/Interceptor, TIE Bomber and Millennium Falcon
Full flight control on the controllers, remappable in the game's controller options
Laser pointer for the concourse, hangar and in-flight menus
Virtual keyboard for pilot names and other text fields
Menus over passthrough on Meta Quest
Controller vibration
needs: Meta Quest 3 (tested) or Quest 2 / 3S / Pro, or PICO 4 / 4 Ultra / Neo 3 (untested)
Your own copy of *Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance* (Steam or GOG)
install: Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r OpenXWA-VR-v0.1.7-beta.apk`.
Copy your whole X-Wing Alliance game folder (the one with `STRINGS.TXT`) to the headset's internal storage as `OpenXWA`, so that `/sdcard/OpenXWA/STRINGS.TXT` exists.
Start **OpenXWA VR** from *Unknown Sources* and allow "access to all files" when asked.
Optional: to make hyperspace selectable in *Options → Game Controller Options*, add the line `!KEY_H!104 H Hyperspace` to `/sdcard/OpenXWA/JOYSTICK.TXT`.

rows: Roll (left/right), throttle lever (up/down, stays where you leave it)
Target the craft in your sights
Pick up targeted cargo / release carried cargo
Left grip + left / right stick click
Dock with / board the targeted craft

games.controls_note: Button names are those of the Meta Quest controllers; PICO controllers use the same layout.
notes: The APK contains no game data: you need your own copy of the game.
The small screens built into the X-Wing Revival cockpits are dark. All other craft (and gunner seats) keep X-Wing Alliance's own cockpits with their live screens.
Passthrough behind the menus works on Meta Quest only; on PICO the menus float in front of black.
Ambient occlusion is off in VR; the GPU runs close to its limit in busy scenes.
PICO needs **PICO OS 5.9.0 or newer**: only from that version does the PICO runtime work with the generic Khronos OpenXR loader the port uses.

The PICO build is untested: if it does not start, or the controllers do nothing, please open an issue on GitHub. `adb logcat -s SDL/APP:*` shows how far it gets, which is the useful thing to paste in.

games.name: FreeSpace 2 VR
games.tagline: The space combat classic FreeSpace 2 in stereo 3D, standalone on Meta Quest and PICO.
about: A VR port of *FreeSpace 2*, running standalone on the [FreeSpace Open](https://github.com/scp-fs2open/fs2open.github.com) engine. Space is rendered in stereo around you, the HUD floats in front of your ship and lines up with your guns, and the menus, briefings and cutscenes play on a big virtual screen. Bring your own copy of the game from GOG or Steam.
PICO support is brand new and **not tested on PICO hardware yet**: reports are very welcome. One APK covers both makes.
features: Head-tracked stereo 3D space in flight
HUD fixed in front of the ship, with crosshair, target brackets and lead indicators lined up with your guns
Full flight control on the controllers: throttle lever on the right stick, a second button layer on the left grip, remappable in *Options → Controls*
Training missions playable with the controllers
Chase view behind your ship
Full lighting with ship shine, environment reflections and anti-aliasing
Laser pointer for the menus, skippable cutscenes
Laser keyboard for typing your pilot callsign
Runs on PICO 4 / Neo 3 too, from the same APK (untested)
needs: Meta Quest 3 (tested) or Quest 2 / 3S / Pro (untested), or PICO 4 / Neo 3 (untested)
Your own copy of FreeSpace 2 ([GOG](https://www.gog.com/game/freespace_2) or [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/273620/)), about 1.8 GB of game files
install: Sideload the APK with SideQuest or `adb install -r -g FreeSpace2-VR-v0.1.2-beta.apk`. SideQuest is a Quest tool, so on PICO use adb or whichever sideloader you already use.

Hold the weapon with both hands

games.name: TrackMania Nations Forever VR
games.tagline: The classic stunt racer from the cockpit, standalone on Meta Quest 3.
about: jiink's TrackMania Forever VR mod (TMFOXR), rebuilt to run **standalone on Meta Quest 3** through WinlatorXR (Wine + Box64 + DXVK). Races are in stereo 3D with head tracking. The main menu stays on WinlatorXR's sharp flat screen, and VR switches on by itself when a race starts. Beta 0.2 adds a **ready-made container image**: import it, and it downloads the free game from Nadeo and sets everything up.
features: Stereoscopic 3D races with head tracking, 1728×1728 per eye, 4x antialiasing
Cockpit camera with the car's own dashboard
VR only while racing: the main menu stays flat and sharp, while the pause, medal and finish screens stay in VR
Quest controllers as a gamepad with analog steering; nothing to bind in the game
The game follows the WinlatorXR screen size automatically
needs: Meta Quest 3
WinlatorXR Dawn
Internet on the first start: the image downloads TrackMania Nations Forever (free, 530 MB) from Nadeo
Only for the manual packages: TrackMania Nations Forever and the [TMLoader](https://tomashu.dev/software/tmloader/) "prepackaged" mod loader
install: **Easiest (container image):** download `TrackMania-VR-Beta-0.2.tzst` to the headset. In WinlatorXR, go to Containers → menu → **Import** and pick it.

Start the **TrackMania VR** shortcut with the headset on. On the first start it downloads TrackMania Nations Forever from Nadeo's official server, installs it and starts the game. The main menu appears flat, and VR starts with the race.
Recommended: lower the graphics quality once in `C:\TmForever\TmForeverLauncher.exe` (Settings). It raised races from about 23 to 30–45 fps.

**Manual alternative (Dawn):** copy your TrackMania folder to `Download/TmForever` with the TMLoader "prepackaged" zip, unzip `TMFOXR-Quest-Dawn-Beta-0.2.zip` into it and import the included `TMFOXR-VR.wxrprofile.json`. Set the DX wrapper to **DXVK 2.4 with Async** by hand. See `README_DAWN.txt`.
**Manual alternative (cats-27, untested):** run `install.cmd` from `TMFOXR-Quest-Installer-Beta-0.2.zip` inside your container. See `README_INSTALL.txt`.
notes: The container image contains no game files; the game comes from Nadeo's server on the first start. Offline, put Nadeo's `tmnationsforever_setup.exe` into the headset's `Download` folder first.
Races run at about 30–45 fps. The limit is TrackMania's main thread under Box64, so lower graphics quality helps most.
Use a 2:1 screen size (3456x1728, 2880x1440 or 1920x1080); WinlatorXR crashed with screens wider than about 3500 pixels.
Short stutters the first time new objects appear, while shaders compile; DXVK async reduces them.
Only TrackMania **Nations** Forever (Stadium) was tested.
Play with more than 50% battery; the Quest throttles below that.

games.name: Bugdom VR
games.tagline: Pangea's 1999 bug adventure in stereo 3D, standalone on Meta Quest.
about: [Bugdom](https://github.com/jorio/Bugdom), Pangea Software's 1999 3D platformer in Iliyas Jorio's modern port, running natively on Meta Quest through OpenXR. You play Rollie McFly, a pill bug out to free the ladybugs from King Thorax.

The world is rendered in stereo 3D around you, with the chase camera behind Rollie and the horizon kept level. The HUD floats on a panel in front of you, and menus are point-and-click with the controller laser.
The game data is free and comes inside the APK, so there is nothing else to copy. PICO support is built in but **not tested on PICO hardware yet**: reports are very welcome.
features: Stereoscopic 3D with head tracking, 4x antialiasing
Chase camera with a level horizon and 30° snap turns
Recenter: automatic on start, or hold the right stick click for 1 second (sets forward and eye height, seated or standing)
In-game HUD bars moved toward the edges of your view, so they don't cover the action
Point-and-click menus with the right controller's laser
Correct colors (sRGB output, no washed-out look)
One APK for Quest and PICO; game data included
needs: Meta Quest 2 / Pro / 3 / 3S (Quest 3 tested), or PICO 4 / Neo 3 (untested)
install: Enable developer mode on your headset.
Download the APK below.
Sideload it with [SideQuest](https://sidequestvr.com/setup-howto) or `adb install -r Bugdom-VR-1.3.5-beta1.apk`. On PICO use adb or whichever sideloader you already use.
Launch *Bugdom* from *Library → Unknown Sources* on Quest, or from your library on PICO.
games.controls_note: Button names are those of the Meta Quest controllers; PICO controllers use the same layout.
notes: This is the first public beta, tested on Quest 3. Please report problems on GitHub.
PICO needs **PICO OS 5.9.0 or newer**: only from that version does the PICO runtime work with the generic Khronos OpenXR loader the port uses.
The APK is signed with a debug key (sideload only).
